description.narrative:
Project outcomes for the Project include: Stakeholder effects: (i) Effects on consumers - The Project is expected to supply up to 1,940 affordable housing units within the investment period by a developer who is increasingly going down-market. The increase in access to quality housing at lower-priced points will help address the shortage of housing in Kenya and benefit families who currently cannot afford quality housing in the market; (ii) Effects on suppliers - With a larger scale of construction, there will be an increase in demand for building materials; (iii) Effects on local communities - those who live in the area will benefit from urban infrastructure such as roads, electricity, water and sanitation that were developed as a result of the Project. Economy-wide effects: The Project will create direct and indirect jobs through the construction of the housing projects. Local suppliers of building materials and other services will also benefit from the increased demand. The Government of Kenya may also benefit from higher tax payments from imports and company income. Environmental effects: Reaching efficiency in residential housing is an important step towards addressing climate change. Globally buildings account for 40% of GHG emissions and are an important consumer of energy. The Project is expected to improve energy efficiency, reducing GHG emissions. All developments will use EDGE standards requiring a minimum of 20% savings on water usage, energy usage, and embodied energy.
The Projects contribution to market creation includes: Competitiveness: The market for affordable housing in Kenya is underdeveloped. The limited provision of affordable housing is primarily driven by supply-side constraints due to: (i) high building costs and regulatory costs for approval processes; and (ii) limited access to finance for developers. The Project will demonstrate to other developers that good quality housing can be profitable and successful in a more affordable market segment, which could lead to more investments in the sector.

The proposed IFC investment is an up to US$20 million A Loan (the Loan) to support Centum Real Estate Limited (CRE, the Company), a wholly owned subsidiary of Centum Investment Company Plc (CIC, the Sponsor), to finance its development of 1,940 affordable housing units in Two Rivers Development (Two Rivers), a prime mixed use urban node located within Kenyas Diplomatic Blue Zone in northern Nairobi (the Project). The Project will address the obvious and increasing affordable housing market gap in Kenya.
